title: Youth-media-protection and accessibility baseline for a German public knowledge website whose declared audience is young adults
question: Which binding German and EU requirements govern a public, German-language knowledge website whose declared audience is young adults — youth media protection (JMStV, BzKJ/KJM, Jugendmedienschutz), minors' data protection (DSGVO Art. 8 with the German age of consent of 16 and guardian consent), and Barrierefreiheit (BFSG, BITV 2.0, EN 301 549, WCAG 2.2 AA) — and what do the responsible official bodies and the empirical literature on age-appropriate design establish about how such a site must label content, handle accounts and analytics for under-18 users, and make itself accessible, so that endia.de is built compliantly from the start rather than retrofitted after launch?
why_now: README.md declares endia.de to be the 'Website zur Buchreihe Endia — eine Young-Adult-Trilogie' and the ecosystem's knowledge-platform, but the repository is still an empty skeleton (README plus empty external-tasks folders). Every later architectural choice — accounts and progress, gamification, comments or community features, analytics, embedded media — inherits these constraints, and the onboarding rules already require the project to report whether it processes personal data and to state deletion timelines. The BFSG obligations for consumer-facing digital services have applied since 2025-06-28, and the ecosystem commits to systemwide AI transparency for public publications (ECO-ARC-0028), so this is a current legal baseline, not a hypothetical one.
real_world_anchor: JMStV and BzKJ/KJM youth-media-protection regime; DSGVO/GDPR Art. 8 with the German implementation setting the age of consent at 16; DDG § 5 (Impressum) for public German sites; BFSG (in force since 2025-06-28) with BITV 2.0, EN 301 549 and WCAG 2.2 AA as the technical reference standards; comparative: ICO Age Appropriate Design Code as an official-institution benchmark.
